lines.text: We came home eighteen days after we left. The whole village was waiting at the north gate.
The moment my boots touched green grass again, I felt them. A hundred and twelve threads, snapping close, like a door opening on a warm room.
My lord. You look terrible.
Thank you, Bram. I missed you too.
Your hands.
Better than they were. Is everyone all right?
Ilse shook hands with half the village that afternoon. Nobody had grown. Not a hair. But nobody had slipped, either.
Exactly where you left them. Dough in a cold kitchen.
At the gate, Garrow stood as if it were the edge of a cliff.
Wren's mother came out of the crowd, and looked at him for a long time.
Then she slapped him. Then she held onto him, and wouldn't let go. Then she slapped him again.
I deserved that.
You deserved worse. I still have your bowl.
And then Ash came through the gate. With company.
The white wolf walked in beside him as if she owned the place. Half the village backed away. Every child ran straight at her.
She is carrying his pups, lord.
How can you possibly know that?
Skeld know.
Absolutely not.
Bram, she's...
Absolutely not.
An hour later, Bram was building her a kennel beside the keep, muttering, with one arm.
That night, I went into the hall to look at the lamp.
It had dimmed. Only a little. You'd only notice if you had looked at it every night for a year.
There was frost on the north field this morning, my lord. First time since spring.
Eighteen days away, and the cold was already creeping back. And any day now, two hundred Skeld would be living on that field, trusting me to keep it warm.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter forty-two, coming soon.
